AGENDA
  CITY COUNCIL MEETING
  FEBRUARY 5, 2019
REGULAR MEETING
  6:00 PM
  NORWALK CITY HALL/COUNCIL CHAMBERS
  AND VIA VIDEOCONFERENCE

  Jennifer Perez, Mayor
  Margarita L. Rios, Vice Mayor
  Tony Ayala, Councilmember
  Leonard Shryock, Councilmember
  Luigi Vernola, Councilmember
  Public Comment: Comments may be made in person, submitted via email at: publiccomments@norwalkca.gov, or through
  the video conference during the designated time on any item on the agenda or on any other matter within the jurisdiction
  subject to the rules of decorum described in Norwalk Municipal Code §2.08.020. The maximum time allowed is three
  minutes.

  Pursuant to provisions of the Brown Act, no action may be taken on a matter unless it is listed on the agenda, or unless
  certain emergency or special circumstances exist. The City Council may direct staff to investigate and/or schedule certain
  matters for consideration at a future City Council meeting.

  Please adhere to the following procedures when addressing the Council:

  • Comments should be limited to 3 minutes or less.
  • Comments should be directed to the City Council as a whole and not directed to individual Councilmembers.

  Americans with Disabilities Act: In compliance with the ADA, if you need special assistance to participate in a City
  meeting or other services offered by this City, please contact the City Clerk's Department, (562) 929-5720. Assisted listening
  devices are available at this meeting. Ask the City Clerk if you desire to use this device. Upon request, the agenda and
  documents in the agenda packet can be made available in appropriate alternative formats to persons with a disability.
  Notification of at least 48 hours prior to the meeting or time when services are needed will assist the City staff in assuring
  that reasonable arrangements can be made to provide accessibility to the meeting or service.

  Note: Any writings and/or documents provided to a majority of the City Council regarding any item on this agenda after it
  has been posted will also be made available for public inspection.

  Writings and/or documents are available for inspection in the City Clerk's Department, City Hall, 12700 Norwalk Boulevard
  during regular business hours, 8:00 a.m. to 6:00 p.m., Monday - Thursday and 8:00 a.m. to 5:00 p.m., every other Friday;
  telephone (562) 929-5720. You may also contact the City Clerk via e mail at recordsrequests@norwalkca.gov.

CALL TO ORDER
  Mayor Perez

ROLL CALL
  Theresa Devoy, CMC
  City Clerk

ORAL COMMUNICATIONS FOR CLOSED SESSION MATTERS
 CLOSED SESSION

  I.  CONFERENCE WITH REAL PROPERTY NEGOTIATOR PURSUANT TO GOVERNMENT CODE
  §54956.8, Assessor Parcel Numbers 8054-016-901, 8054-016-903, 8054-016-904, 8054-016-905, and
  8054-016-906; Negotiating on behalf of the City: Jesus Gomez, City Manager; Negotiating Party:
  Mercy Housing; Under Negotiation: Price and Terms of Payment.

  II.  CONFERENCE WITH REAL PROPERTY NEGOTIATOR PURSUANT TO GOVERNMENT CODE
  §54956.8, Assessor Parcel Numbers 8047-006-924 and 8047-006-925; Negotiating on behalf of the
  City: Jesus Gomez, City Manager; Negotiating Party: Primestor; Under Negotiation: Price and Terms of
  Payment.

  III.  CONFERENCE WITH REAL PROPERTY NEGOTIATOR PURSUANT TO GOVERNMENT CODE
  §54956.8: Assessor Parcel Number 8045-008-902; Negotiating on behalf of the City: Jesus Gomez,
  City Manager; Negotiating Party: State of California; Under Negotiation: Price and Terms of Payment.

  IV.  CONFERENCE WITH REAL PROPERTY NEGOTIATOR PURSUANT TO GOVERNMENT CODE
  §54956.8: Assessor Parcel Number 8082-013-905; Negotiating on behalf of the City: Jesus Gomez,
  City Manager; Negotiating Party: Department of the Air Force; Under Negotiation: Price and Terms of
  Payment.

RECESS

  REGULAR MEETING – 6:00 p.m.

CALL TO ORDER
  Mayor Perez

INVOCATION
  Pastor Richard Butterfield
  Community Chapel World Outreach Church

FLAG SALUTE
  Rachel Alvarado, 8th grade
  Lakeside Middle School

ROLL CALL
  Theresa Devoy, CMC
  City Clerk

CITY COUNCIL COMMENTS

  a.  Report of City Council Travel

SPECIAL PRESENTATIONS

  I.  City Council to recognize Marc Anthony Rivas for achieving the Eagle Court of Honor in the Boy Scouts
  of America.

  II.  City Council to recognize Hometown Heroes from the City of Norwalk.

  III.  City Council to recognize Norwalk Sheriff Deputies David Pantoja, Perla Escalera, Bryan Cendejas,
  Brew Lopez, Jon Balarosan, Jeremy Licona and Detectives Carl Anna, Alan Hernandez, Jose Lopez,
  and German Ochoa, for their professional commitment to excellence in community policing in Norwalk.

CITY MANAGER COMMENTS

  I.  Recap swearing in ceremony for Senator Bob Archuleta.

  II.  2020 Census Update.
   CLOSED SESSION REPORT

CONSENT CALENDAR

Consent calendar items are considered routine matters which may be enacted by one motion and roll call vote.
Any item may be removed from the consent calendar and considered separately by City Council.

  1.  MEETING MINUTES – Staff recommends City Council approve the minutes of the meetings of
  January 15 and 19, 2019. 825-04

  Minutes

  2.  PAYROLL – Staff recommends City Council approve the payroll for the periods December 16, 2018 –
  December 29, 2018, in the total amount of $972,856.45 and December 30, 2018 – January 12, 2019,
  in the total amount of $909,640.13. 630

  Report

  3.  COMMERCIAL DEMANDS – Staff recommends City Council approve the warrant register dated
  January 9, 2019 through January 29, 2019, in the total amount of $2,998,292.12. 640

  Warrants

  4.  CLAIMS AGAINST THE CITY – Staff recommends City Council deny the claims filed by Allstate
  Insurance, Ramiro Chacon, and Jeremy Corley. 830-01/03

  Report

  5.  PLANNING COMMISSION SYNOPSIS – JANUARY 23, 2019 - No action is required unless the City
  Council elects to review the decision of the Planning Commission on those items where the
  Commission’s action was final. 320

  Report

  6.  APPROVAL OF NORWALK SENIOR CITIZENS CENTER INC. (NSCC INC.) BOARD OF DIRECTORS
  – Staff recommends City Council approve the nominations of Julie Duran, President; Jennie Javier,
  Vice President; Carol Hackworth, Treasurer; Bobbie Wakefield, Secretary; and Diane Richards, Board
  Member to the NSCC Inc. Board of Directors for one-year terms to expire December 31, 2019. 420-02-
  04

  Report

  7.  AGREEMENT AMENDMENT – BUS MAINTENANCE CONSULTING – Staff recommends City Council
  approve Amendment No. 2 to the agreement with AP Bus Maintenance Consulting increasing the total
  amount from $51,000 to $81,000; and authorize the City Manager to execute Amendment No. 2 and
  any other amendments provided there is funding in the budget, on behalf of the City, in a form
  approved by the City Attorney. 1120-10

  Report

  8.  AGREEMENT – BUS UPGRADES – Staff recommends City Council approve an agreement with
  Complete Coach Works (CCW) for upgrading the Advantac Heating Ventilation Air Conditioning
  (HVAC) Bus Rooftop Units in the amount of $285,171.39, as a sole source procurement for this project;
  and authorize the City Manager to execute the agreement and any other amendments provided there
  is funding in the budget, on behalf of the City, in a form approved by the City Attorney. 634-03

  Report

  9.  REQUEST TO USE CIVIC CENTER LAWN FOR A CARNIVAL – Staff recommends City Council
  approve the carnival requested by the Norwalk Float Foundation for the dates of March 6 through
  March 10, 2019 and waive security deposit and fees as requested consistent with past practice. 920-
  01-02
   Report

APPOINTMENTS

  10. ADVISORY BODIES – Staff recommends City Council make appointments to fill the vacancies on the
  various City advisory bodies. 200

  Report

REPORTS

  11. COMPREHENSIVE ANNUAL FINANCIAL REPORT (CAFR) FOR FISCAL YEAR ENDING JUNE 30,
  2018 – Receive and file. 610

  Report

  12. FEDERAL TRANSIT ADMINISTRATION (FTA) FISCAL YEAR (FY) 17 5339 BUS AND BUS
  FACILITIES BUDGET ALLOCATION AND PARTNERSHIP DISSOLUTION WITH THE ANAHEIM
  TRANSIT NETWORK (ATN) – Staff recommends City Council authorize:

  a.  the dissolution of the Norwalk Transit System/ATN FTA joint application; and

  b.  the City Manager to execute all necessary documents on behalf of the City of Norwalk to process
  the dissolution from ATN in order to file FTA grant and claim the full award of federal funds. 1105-
  01

  Report

  13. UPDATE ON AFFORDABLE HOUSING PROJECT FOR VETERANS – Receive and file. 920-11

  Report

  14. EXCLUSIVE NEGOTIATING AGREEMENT FOR THE DEVELOPMENT OF THE CIVIC CENTER
  PLAZA – Staff recommends City Council approve an Exclusive Negotiating Agreement with Primestor
  Development, Inc. to establish the terms and conditions of a ground lease for Civic Center Plaza; and
  authorize the City Manager to execute the agreement and any amendments provided there is funding
  in budget, on behalf of the City, in a form approved by the City Attorney. 920-01

  Report

  15. EXCLUSIVE NEGOTIATING AGREEMENT FOR THE DEVELOPMENT OF THE CALIFORNIA YOUTH
  AUTHORITY PROPERTY – Staff recommends City Council approve an Exclusive Negotiating
  Agreement with Lewis Acquisition Company, LLC (Lewis Management Corp.) to assist the City in tasks
  required for the development of California Youth Authority property; and authorize the City Manager to
  execute the agreement and any amendments provided there is funding in budget, on behalf of the City,
  in a form approved by the City Attorney. 940-01

  Report

ORAL COMMUNICATIONS

ADJOURNMENT

I hereby certify under penalty of perjury under the laws of the State of California that the foregoing agenda was posted
on the City Hall bulletin board not less than 72 hours prior to the meeting. Dated February 1, 2019.

Theresa Devoy, CMC
City Clerk
